deep.reconstruction:
Purpose. The page is a scrap that doubles as a library or reading note. The ink header lists Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik und Chemie: second series vols. 70–74 plus Ergänzungsband 1, and third series vols. 10–14. Large pencil notes repeat these ('1842', 'W. 70.74', '3 v. 10.14'). It is signed 'B. Riemann (Agel)' and dated in red 'Febr. 7.56'. The mathematics is a short study of one integral of the form ψ = ∫_α^∞ e^{-(ps+q/s)} ds/s, or a close variant. Minus signs in the exponent are clearly intended for convergence, though the ink often omits them. The integral is a lower-truncated ('incomplete') Laplace-type integral with exponent ps+q/s. Such integrals arise from heat or diffusion kernels with leakage, e.g. ∫ e^{-x²/(4t)-kt} t^{-ν} dt, the kind of integral needed in the 1850s electrical problems (cable or residual-charge diffusion) that Riemann studied in Poggendorff's Annalen.

Step 1 (completing the square, ink 'ψ e^{2√pq}' and '∫ e^{(√(sp)+√(q/s))²}'). For s>0 one has (√(sp)+√(q/s))² = sp + q/s + 2√(pq). Hence e^{-(sp+q/s)} = e^{2√(pq)} · e^{-(√(sp)+√(q/s))²}. Therefore ψ·e^{-2√pq}, written ψ e^{2√pq} with the sign convention lost, equals ∫ e^{-(√(sp)+√(q/s))²}(…)ds. The measure is unclear ('∂ I'). This is the classical device for reducing ∫e^{-ps-q/s} s^{-1/2}ds and ∫e^{-ps-q/s} s^{-3/2}ds to the error function.

Step 2 (substitution t = √(sp)+√(q/s)). The lower limit becomes t = √(αp)+√(q/α), exactly as written on the page. The integral becomes a Gaussian tail ∫_{√(αp)+√(q/α)}^∞ e^{-t²} dt, matching the ink '∫^∞ e^{t²}∂t' with lower limit √(αp)+√(q/α). [My completion: this is exact for the combination of the s^{-1/2} and s^{-3/2} weights that makes dt appear. The twin substitution √(sp)−√(q/s) gives the other combination.]

Step 3 (alternative substitution σ = sp + q/s). Inverting gives s = (σ ± √(σ²−4pq))/(2p). The page writes (s ± √(s²−pq))/√p, apparently with a rescaled variable, e.g. sp+q/s = 2σ for √p·s. Differentiating, (p − q/s²) ds = dσ. Since ps − q/s = ±√(σ²−4pq), we get ds/s = ± dσ/√(σ²−4pq). On the monotone branch s ≥ √(q/p), i.e. α ≥ √(q/p): ψ = ∫_α^∞ e^{-(ps+q/s)} ds/s = ∫_{αp+q/α}^∞ e^{-σ} dσ/√(σ²−4pq). This is exactly the last formula on the page.

As α→0 (both branches) the integral gives the Macdonald representation 2K_0(2√pq) = ∫_{2√pq}^∞ e^{-σ}·2dσ/√(σ²−4pq).

Figure. A rectangle ruled into a grid, with corner labels 0 and ∞. It is probably a sketch of the integration region or the change of variables (s from 0 to ∞, split at the critical point s = √(q/p)).
errors: Signs of the exponents are not written consistently: convergence requires e^{-(sp+q/s)}, e^{-(√(sp)+√(q/s))²}, e^{-t²}. Hence the identity should read ψ e^{-2√pq} = ∫ e^{-(√(sp)+√(q/s))²}…, not ψ e^{+2√pq}, unless ψ was defined with the opposite sign convention.

The inverse '(s ± √(s²−pq))/√p' does not match the final integral's √(s²−4pq) under the same normalization. For σ = ps+q/s the root is (σ ± √(σ²−4pq))/(2p). The page formula corresponds to a rescaled variable; this is not an error if the normalization changed, but it is inconsistent as written.

The reduction ∫_α^∞ e^{-(ps+q/s)}ds/s = ∫_{αp+q/α}^∞ e^{-σ}dσ/√(σ²−4pq) holds only if α ≥ √(q/p), where σ(s) is monotone. For smaller α the interval must be split into two branches. The page does not state this.
The measure in the first integral is not legible ('∂ I'), so the exact weight (ds/s vs ds/√s) cannot be confirmed.

results.what: Completing the square sp+q/s = (√(sp)+√(q/s))² − 2√(pq), reducing ∫e^{-ps-q/s} integrals to a Gaussian tail (error function) with lower limit √(αp)+√(q/α)
results.modern_name: Reduction of ∫e^{-a²x²-b²/x²}-type integrals to erfc (Laplace/Cauchy substitution)
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace (c.1782–1810); standard in Cauchy and in heat-conduction literature

results.what: Substitution σ = ps + q/s turning the truncated integral into ∫_{αp+q/α}^∞ e^{-σ}dσ/√(σ²−4pq)
results.modern_name: Incomplete modified Bessel (Macdonald) function K_0; integral representation K_0(z) = ∫_1^∞ e^{-zu}/√(u²−1) du
results.usually_credited_to: Representation of K_0: Poisson/Basset/Macdonald (19th c.); incomplete Bessel functions studied much later (20th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard substitutions for Laplace-type integrals with exponent ps+q/s, familiar to anyone working on heat or electrical diffusion in the 1850s. The page is a scratch computation on a library/reference slip. Its interest is mainly biographical: it is dated Feb 1856 and points to Poggendorff's Annalen in connection with Riemann's physics work.

transcription_corrections: '∫^∞ e^{t²}∂t' should be read with an intended minus sign, e^{-t²}; the lower limit √(αp)+√(q/α) belongs to this integral.
The first formula likely reads ψ = ∫_α^∞ e^{-(sp+q/s)}…; the upper limit is overwritten, and the struck item after it is a cancelled differential.
'(s ± √(s²−pq))/√p': the leading symbol under the overwrite appears to be 's' with a superscript correction; it is an inverse-substitution root, with a normalization differing from the final 4pq.

The pencil note '3 2' at left is probably '32', a large page or volume number. The pencil 'Einzelbl.' reading is uncertain; it may be a word like 'Ergänzbd.' (Ergänzungsband), consistent with the ink header.
Final integral: the lower limit is αp + q/α (the 'q/α' is overwritten), and the integrand is e^{-s} ds/√(s²−4pq).
